evidence.text: Integrate solutions satisfying the respective endpoint conditions and locate eigenvalues through zeros of their Wronskian, evaluated at theta=pi/2. Scan background initial data to obtain the first positive eigenvalue as a function over the admissible domain.

sources.title: On the spin-2 Kaluza-Klein spectrum of $ {\mathrm{AdS}}_4\times {S}^2\left({\mathrm{\mathcal{B}}}_4\right) $

evidence.text: Numerically integrate the background using a=exp(2A), c=exp(2C), retaining globally bounded nonnegative solutions. Mathematica's Backward Differentiation Formula addresses equatorial instabilities. Alternative initial data near theta=pi/2 use a local expansion with an offset of order 10^-4.

sources.title: On the spin-2 Kaluza-Klein spectrum of $ {\mathrm{AdS}}_4\times {S}^2\left({\mathrm{\mathcal{B}}}_4\right) $

evidence.text: Restrict to modes depending only on theta. Their equation is (p g')'+lambda q g=0, with p=exp[4(A+C)] sin(theta)/f and q=exp[4(A+C)] f sin(theta). The paper maps this singular problem using g_tilde=g/u, u=1-log(sin theta), to what it identifies as a regular Sturm-Liouville problem.

evidence.text: Flux quantization is inverted using B-shift-invariant integer combinations, including n2²−2n0n4 and n2³+3n0²n6−3n0n2n4. For N=2, pure-spinor supersymmetry equations reduce to three first-order ODEs; pole expansions and numerical matching determine the regular symmetric family.

evidence.text: A timelike-frame component of the string-frame Einstein equation expresses a two-derivative NS–NS combination, multiplied by e^(−2φ), as a sum of nonnegative electric and magnetic RR-flux squares. Quantization supplies a nonzero lower scale through F0.
